$about: The size system of the site: every fluid size comes from this file and nowhere else. build/tokens.mjs reads it (npm run tokens, and before every dev and build), checks its rules and writes one CSS formula per size into src/styles/base/tokens.gen.css.

One range for everything: a size has its value on a 320px screen and on a 1440px one, a straight line in between, constant outside. Above 1440 nothing grows any more; the content column stops at 1520px and wide screens get wider margins (the Figma frames of 1920 and 2560 do the same).

A screen counts as only as big as its height allows (range.height): a screen 360px tall gets the sizes of a 320 screen, one 920px tall the sizes of a 1440 screen, a straight line in between. So a phone turned sideways gets the phone sizes and a 1366 × 650 laptop window the sizes of a 900px screen, all sizes together.
One ladder for every size, type and space alike: steps of 2 up to 24, of 4 up to 64, of 8 up to 128, of 16 up to 256. Both ends of every role sit on it.

Type: two families. Mono (PT Mono Bold, upper case, tracked 0.05em) for names and headings; sans (Apercu Pro) for everything you read. The levels in type.relations stay at least ×1.125 apart at both ends of the range, and so at every size between.
No radius anywhere: QQ is drawn in sharp rectangles and hairlines (the brandbook's grid). Only pills (descriptors, steppers) and dots are round. Not a token: a rule (build/rules.mjs).

type/hero.use: the home hero's title «Кофе свежей обжарки»: below L at this size, at most two words a line; from L it fills its cell between 48 and this (Tim, round 6: 48 at least, on the ladder)

type/display.use: the titles of the business and about pages' heroes (the home hero's own was this until round 6)

type/h2.use: section headings, the catalog tabs, the product's name on its page

type/h3.use: headings of the image blocks (approach, about)

type/title.use: the name of the featured coffee

type/card-title.use: names on product cards, titles of tiles (business, info blocks, product facts), footer headings

type/label.use: eyebrows above headings («Наш подход»): set apart by colour and case, not size

type/statement.use: the big sentence of a product's story

type/lead.use: the caption over the featured photo, the text under a section heading

type/body-l.use: longer text: the featured description, the story columns, business text

type/body.use: card descriptions, lists, links of the navbar and the footer, fields

type/small.use: descriptor pills, captions above values in the buy bar, the copyright

type/control.use: big actions and values set in bold capitals: hero links, «В корзину», buy-bar values

type/price.use: prices and weights on cards (medium capitals)

relations.$about: Neighbouring levels that must stay apart at both ends of the range. Not here, on purpose: labels (case and colour set them apart) and the countdown (a figure, not text).

page/gutter.use: side margin of every section: the content column starts here

section/pad-y.use: space above and below a section's content

section/pad-y-s.use: the tighter edge of a section that follows a related one (new arrivals → recommended)

section/gap.use: from a section heading to its content

grid/row-gap.use: between rows of product cards (each card carries a description below it)

block/pad.use: padding of big blocks: the featured text card, the text of image blocks, info blocks

tile/pad.use: padding of tiles: product facts, business descriptions, filter cells

control/h.use: height of the card's buy row and of big buttons

control/pad-x.use: side padding of buttons and controls

hero/cell-y.use: padding above and below each row of the hero's cells (three rows: the roast's parts beside the three links)

hero/photo.use: the least photo the hero shows between the navbar and the fade into its cells

fact/icon.use: the icon of an info block and of its modal (roasting, payment, delivery): larger on larger screens (Tim, round 5)

hero/fade.use: the eased fade from the hero's photo into the black of its cells

hero/max.use: the most the hero may be tall: below it, the screen less a 24px peek (a tall portrait or 2560 screen stops here)

story/min-h.use: least height of the image blocks (approach, about)

footer/logo.use: width of the flame mark in the footer

modal/w.use: width of a modal (an info block opened); under 40em (the tab bar's step) a modal is a sheet as wide as the screen

product/stage.use: the 3D pack on a product page: the side of its square (also capped by the screen's height)

steps.$about: The widths at which blocks change their layout: container queries on the content column, shared by every block. Named by what they are, in rem (a visitor's bigger text makes the column count as narrower). M and L leave room for a classic scrollbar at 768 and 1024. max is the column at its most (--col-max, in px as it is): from there on the margins grow, and a full-width block may frame its column.
